scope: Restricted CPU executor only; not a general platform or GPU-runtime security approval.
critical_policy: Any Critical finding blocks deployment. No suppressed findings.
conditions: Dedicated platform-ops namespace with restricted Pod admission.
Mutual TLS only; fixed typed API; no submitted commands or credential paths.
UID/GID 20002; no capabilities, escalation, host namespaces/devices or writable root.
Private retained EFS access point; SSH and workload credentials excluded from management Pods.
Exact six-host SSM start scope and own-session transport/termination only.
One non-retrying Job per task; trusted SSH host keys and expected Kubernetes UID.
No SQLite, Perl-tar, infocmp, privileged local ACL/mount or Go HTTP server workload.
Review expires within seven days and must be renewed for new image, findings or exposure.

high_findings.rationale: The reported entry point is infocmp terminfo analysis. The fixed typed API and worker commands do not invoke infocmp or accept terminfo inputs; locale is fixed. The distribution packages remain affected; terminal/tool exposure changes require a new review.

The locked SSM plugin is currently the latest official release and retains an older Go verifier. Its only authorized outbound peer is the fixed AWS SSM endpoint; scoped IAM, TLS verification and URL validation narrow exposure. Untrusted-intermediate handling remains a residual dependency risk. Rebuild/upgrade and rescan when a supported patched release is available; the retained runc artifact is not executed locally.

Executor state uses typed JSON files; it does not execute caller SQL or open submitted SQLite/FTS5 databases. Management persistence is PostgreSQL outside this service. SQLite remains affected and no general SQL/file-processing API is authorized by this review.

Only systemd/udev libraries are listed in this runtime scan, not a running systemd-homed service. PID 1 is the Python service or fixed worker, with no host/systemd socket mounts or local root. The library finding is retained rather than declared fixed.

The affected x/net DNS parser is reported in the retained runc artifact. That binary is copied to a GPU host by a separate runtime procedure and is not executed by the CPU executor. This review does not authorize unrestricted or live GPU-runtime use of the affected code; GPU runtime compatibility/security requires its own gate.

Path-based privileged ACL manipulation is outside the authored executor commands. The process has no local root or DAC capabilities, no host mounts and a private retained UID-20002 access point. The vulnerable library remains installed; privileged/local ACL usage requires a new review.

Local mount/nsenter privilege paths remain present in distribution packages. Executor runs as UID 20002 with all capabilities dropped, no privilege escalation, no host namespaces/devices and a read-only root. Authored operations never invoke these local mount helpers. The vulnerability is not fixed; changing those boundaries invalidates this review.

The reported Perl Archive::Tar path is not used by this runtime. Source/runtime archives use bounded checksum-verified Python tarfile paths, and tasks cannot submit archive bytes or commands. Perl packages remain affected; enabling Perl archive processing invalidates this review.

The Go TLS server ECH parser is not used by the outbound-only SSM client or by the unexecuted runc artifact in this CPU executor. The mTLS listener is Python/OpenSSL. The affected components remain present; this does not establish GPU-host runtime safety.
